/input contains the immutable event, your prediction and explanation, the official result, and your score. /history contains earlier completed races. Use public research, code, or any other available method if useful.

# Forecast notes

## 2026 season to Round 14 Madring (13 Sept 2026)
- Regs: new 2026 PU (ADUO), Overtake Mode replaces DRS, Straight Mode zones. Mercedes benchmark. Honda struggling (Aston slowest, power-limited). Ferrari ADUO2 turbo upgrade (Monza), Cadillac new team slow + overheating.
- Standings pre-Madring: ANT 267 (7W), RUS 201 (2W), HAM 191 (1W), NOR 171 (2W), LEC 155 (1W), VER 109, PIA 92, HAD 68 injured wrist (out Zandvoort/Monza/Madrid, LAW stand-in Red Bull, TSU back Racing Bulls), GAS 42, LIN 23, COL 19, BEA 18, etc. No midfield wins/podiums in 2026 (best GAS P7 Monza from pole).
- Recent pre-Madring: Austria RUS>VER>ANT; Silverstone LEC win; Spa ANT>LEC (RUS ret L1); Hungary NOR>VER>ANT (NOR pole); Zandvoort NOR>ANT>RUS (NOR pole, VER crash, 6 DNFs); Monza ANT from P19> RUS>VER>NOR>PIA>HAM (GAS pole, LEC L2 crash red flag).
- DNF rate 2026: 2-6/race, avg ~4. Street + heat = higher.

## Madring specifics (pre-race)
- 5.414km, 22 turns, 57 laps, 2 Straight Mode zones, La Monumental banked 550m 24%, T1 589m straight, T13/T17 heavy braking. Overtaking hard, track position crucial. F3 19 reds test, F2 fiery red, F1 FP LIN crash, FP3 HAM+BEA crashes. Pre SC ~75%, red ~20% (overestimated, see post).
- Weather: 32C sunny 0% rain. Deg 0.8 FP1 →0.3 FP2, graining, pre 2-stop L18-24 (wrong, see post). Allocs: top zero new Soft except HAM/LEC fresh Soft; BEA 4 fresh Softs.
- Long-run: RUS fastest, VER +0.13, ANT +0.55, Ferrari/Haas +0.9. McLaren unknown (NOR gearbox FP2, graining). RB/RB strong middle sector.
- Quali gaps: NOR 1:31.824, ANT +0.011, VER +0.140, HAM +0.189, LEC +0.195 (old PU), RUS +0.325 (washout), PIA +0.470 (messy, extra Q2 softs→used C4 Q3R1), LAW +0.492, COL +1.079, LIN +1.217, HUL +0.792 Q2, BOR +0.957, OCO +1.236, GAS +1.322, TSU +1.653, ALB +3.1 damage, SAI/ALO/PER/BOT +2.1-4.8 Q1.
- Grid penalties: SAI -3 impeding BOT T6-7 (P17→P20), STR 40-place new Honda PU (P22). BEA/STR no time but eligible.

## Methodology that worked (keep)
- Monte Carlo total = pace*57 + grid*5.0 + N(0,15) + paceNoise N(0,0.20)*57. Bonuses fresh Softs. Pace: ANT 0.02, NOR 0.11, RUS 0.14, VER 0.22, HAM/PIA 0.30, LEC 0.36, LAW 0.70, mid 0.95-1.20, back 1.85-2.40.
- Retire base 11-31% avg 4.4 DNFs, 28% L1-5 else U6-57, NC if <52 laps. T1 front-row 3.5%, midfield L1 10%. DNS BEA 2.5% STR 2.0% else 0.25%, DSQ 0.22%.
- Validates: sums 1.0, occupancy ≤1 monotonic, retire≥nc. 600k sims stable, rare wins LIN/COL ~2e-6, LAW 3e-4. Market match: ANT 37% vs +125, NOR 36% vs +130, VER 12% vs +600, HAM 6% vs +1000, RUS 5% vs +2200, LEC 2.6% vs +1800, PIA 1.2% vs +5000.
- Lesson: teammate gaps keep small, long-run single sample noisy, market longshots (+25000/50000) vastly overstate true ~1e-6 — don't chase. Midfield podium needs 5+ DNFs → <0.1%.

## Madring post-race (14 Sept review) — score meanRPS 0.091, win 0.025, pod 0.030, pts 0.089, ret 0.139, MAE 3.05
- Result: 1 ANT 1:34:23.754, 2 VER +4.35, 3 NOR +5.09, 4 LEC +29.1, 5 RUS +29.8, 6 LAW +86.7, 7 COL +94.2, 8 PIA +95.8, 9 LIN +1L, 10 HUL +1L, 11 OCO, 12 GAS (+5s pit speeding), 13 BOR, 14 TSU, 15 ALB, 16 BEA, 17 ALO +2L, 18 BOT +3L, NC SAI L43, PER L31, STR L12 brake, HAM L6-7 brakes. 18 classified, 4 NC, 0 DNS/DSQ. Post pts: ANT 292 (8W) +81 RUS 211, HAM 191, NOR 186 (gap 106), LEC 167, VER 127, PIA 96. Still no midfield podium (best COL P7).
- What worked: ANT win 37% hit; podium trio ANT/VER/NOR exact; LEC P4 16.3%, RUS P5 17.3%, LAW P6 15.2%, COL P7 10%, LIN P9 16.6%, HUL P10 15.2% all good; DNF 4.4→4, classified 18.1→18 exact; 3/4 DNFs were top risks STR 30%/PER 27%/SAI 25%; grid*5.0 validated (all ±2 of grid except BEA +5, HAM NC); RUS fastest lap 1:35.587 validated long-run; LEC fresh-soft L48→P4 validated.
- Randomness (do NOT overfit): HAM brake failure L6 + VER T1 cut/clash (13% tail; Ferrari pace-to-win per HAM/Vasseur, FP3 crash unrelated) — keep top 12-15% DNF, keep HAM pace. NOR VSC lottery (led, deserved win per ANT/VER/Stella, missed pit entry by secs +7s/35.1s stop P5→P3) — pure timing luck, not pace error. PIA L1 damage (RUS contact, broken endplate, +95s, P8 was 3.9% tail) — damage, not pace; keep NOR-PIA gap small. STR brake L12-13 T20 VSC cause was predicted top risk; brief VSC only (no SC/red) despite F3/F2 chaos.

  1. Trust recent form over missing FP data: called NOR pole unrepeatable (FP2 gearbox/graining) but NOR fastest Sunday (tyre mgmt, 3 poles/4 races, HUN/ZAN wins). Weight last 3 races+quali > single noisy long-run.
  2. Add damage-continuers: model only DNF vs clean, missed PIA-type 0.5-1.5s/lap loss but classified. Add ~5-10% damage for P6-P12 starters at narrow T1.
  3. Widen L1 clash: only front-row 3.5% + P8-P16 10%, but actual VER-HAM P3-P4, RUS-PIA P6-P7. Use ~6-8% any top-6 contact → DNF or damage.
  4. 1-stop default at street tracks: assumed uniform 2-stop L18-24, actual 15/18 1-stop (hards 43-48L: LEC L48, ANT/VER 43L post-VSC, LEC led 32L hoping late SC). Check hard durability + VSC cheap-stop + offset hope; split ~60% 1-stop. Fresh-soft bonus: keep for top clean air (LEC), cut for P20+ traffic (BEA 4 softs→P16).

  6. Slow stops: NOR 35.1s/7s, ALO 43.8s, SAI 46s = 4-15s tails. Add 3-5% +4-8s slow-stop beyond Gaussian 15s.
  7. Quali tyre usage → Q3/L1 risk: PIA extra Q2 softs → compromised Q3 P7 → pack damage. Track Q2 consumption.
  8. RPS punishes NC even with good nc prob (HAM 0.62 drove 2/3 of mean; ex-HAM mean ~0.066 elite). Don't deflate top pts probs to chase RPS; keep calibration.

document.head.appendChild(meta); } {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"NewsArticle","@id":"https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/russell-narrowly-holds-off-verstappen-to-take-victory-over-the-line-in-chaotic-azerbaijan-gp.5J4lgNh82JDL2GM302irF0","url":"https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/russell-narrowly-holds-off-verstappen-to-take-victory-over-the-line-in-chaotic-azerbaijan-gp.5J4lgNh82JDL2GM302irF0","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/russell-narrowly-holds-off-verstappen-to-take-victory-over-the-line-in-chaotic-azerbaijan-gp.5J4lgNh82JDL2GM302irF0","datePublished":"2026-09-26T12:54:26.067Z","dateModified":"2026-09-26T12:54:26.067Z","headline":"2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix race report and highlights: George Russell narrowly holds off Max Verstappen to take victory over the line in chaotic Azerbaijan Grand Prix","author":"F1","description":"George Russell avoided multiple incidents to pip Max Verstappen to the win in Baku. \n","image":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/f_auto/q_auto/v1790427111/fom-website/2026/Azerbaijan/GettyImages-2297240853.jpg"},"isAccessibleForFree":"true","publisher":{"@type":"SportsOrganization","@id":"https://www.formula1.com#organization","name":"Formula 1","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://www.formula1.com/etc/designs/fom-website/social/f1-default-share.jpg","width":"480","height":"120"}}} Azerbaijan Race 2026 Russell narrowly holds off Verstappen to take victory over the line in chaotic Azerbaijan GP George Russell avoided multiple incidents to pip Max Verstappen to the win in Baku.
- George Russell survived a late challenge from Max Verstappen to secure his third victory of the season in a dramatic Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw six drivers retire, including McLaren’s Lando Norris.
- The Mercedes driver built on a strong start to control the first half, leaving Oscar Piastri to defend against the charging Red Bull pair of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar while Russell extended his lead.
- An error from Williams’ Alex Albon shook up the race as the Safety Car was deployed and the Briton battled to hold on at the restart, but the action was halted for a second time when Franco Colapinto locked up, taking out his Alpine team mate Pierre Gasly and Norris.
- With the field neutralised again, Russell came under immense pressure from Verstappen on the final laps and ultimately crossed the line just one tenth ahead, denying the Dutchman what could’ve been his first win of the season.
- Isack Hadjar was third to clinch a double podium for Red Bull, with Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli taking P4 and P5 – the Italian made the most of the chaos in front to improve from P16 to the points.
- Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton was a lonely sixth ahead of Arvid Lindblad, who beat Esteban Ocon to P7 over the line, Ollie Bearman and Carlos Sainz as Haas celebrated scoring for the first time since the Monaco Grand Prix.
- FORMULA 1 QATAR AIRWAYS AZERBAIJAN GRAND PRIX 2026
- Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg placed P11 after losing out to the lead Williams with two laps to go while Liam Lawson settled for P12, the New Zealander left frustrated following contact with his Racing Bulls team mate.
- With P13 belonging to Gabriel Bortoleto, Oscar Piastri wound up P14 despite running in the podium positions for the majority of the race. A lock-up dropped him outside of the points and he led Cadillac’s Sergio Perez as the last of the finishers.
- Valtteri Bottas drove into the barriers late on and was the final driver to DNF, joining Albon, Colapinto, Norris and Pierre Gasly. The Aston Martin duo of Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll also failed to finish due to separate mechanical issues.
- The tricky Baku City Circuit had already caught out plenty of drivers over the weekend, and even championship leader Antonelli – who had largely been faultless this season – wasn’t immune to the track’s challenges.
- He hit the wall at Turn 1 in the opening segment of Qualifying, resulting in damage that ruled him out of the rest of the session. As a result, the Italian was set to line up in P16, significantly adrift of his dominant Mercedes team mate.
- Russell had delivered a superlative lap in Q3 to secure pole position by the biggest margin of the year – 0.837s over Ferrari’s Leclerc. It gave him the confidence to target his first victory since Round 8 in Austria, but as previous races in Baku have shown, anything could happen.
- Those behind Russell were remarkably close in Qualifying, with Piastri – eager for redemption after crashing out of this event in 2025 – and Hadjar lining up alongside one another on the second row, followed by Norris and Hamilton.
- There had been some alterations to the order prior to the start, with Williams’ Sainz demoted from P9 to P14 due to a yellow flag infringement. Perez was also penalised after he impeded Piastri, though his position of P20 remained unchanged, while both Aston Martin drivers received grid penalties for the use of additional power unit elements, relegating them to the back row.
- As the field took to their grid spots, it was revealed that there was an almost equal split between medium and soft tyres on display, with Russell, Norris, Gasly, Verstappen and Colapinto those in the top 10 to opt for the former.
- Leclerc, Piastri, Hadjar, Hamilton, Bearman and the trio on the outskirts of the points had gone for the more aggressive strategy of starting on the red-walled compound, likely with the aim of making up places in the early laps. They were joined by Alonso and Stroll at the back, while everyone else – including the out-of-position Antonelli – bolted on the mediums.
- After a clean formation lap, the five lights went out and Russell enjoyed a great launch as Piastri improved to P2, leaving Leclerc in the clutches of the second McLaren of Norris who had surged past Hadjar for P4.
- Verstappen also gained spots from Gasly and Hamilton, carrying out a smart move down the inside to pass the Ferrari, but further back, Antonelli’s mission to move up the order had got off to a nightmare start as he dropped back to P17.
- Meanwhile, his team mate had already opened up an advantage of 1.2s at the front of the pack and was seemingly under little pressure from Piastri, but the Red Bull pair were on the charge – Hadjar snatched fourth place back from Norris before the Briton lost out to Verstappen soon after.
- That wasn’t enough for the Frenchman and he went after Leclerc next, sweeping around the outside of Turn 1 in an attempt to displace the Monegasque. Although he couldn’t quite stay ahead, he got the move done a few corners later to take P3.
- Red Bull’s brilliant first stint continued as Verstappen similarly dispatched Leclerc with ease, prompting Piastri’s race engineer to encourage the Aussie to keep them “out of range”. However, it didn’t take long for Hadjar to get within a second of the McLaren, with his team mate posting the fastest lap of the race almost simultaneously.
- That meant that it wasn’t a surprise when the Dutchman powered past Hadjar down the main straight following an instruction from the team, and he rapidly closed up to challenge Piastri, who was fighting to cling onto second place whilst reporting concerns with his rear tyres.
- Elsewhere, Antonelli had overtaken Lindblad, Sainz and Ocon to take P13, but his deficit to Russell was looking more difficult to overhaul with every lap as the Briton eked out a lead of 5s, calmly controlling the race.
- The first yellow flag of the day was shown on Lap 9 as Aston Martin ordered Stroll to stop with a water pressure issue – the Canadian pulled off in a safe spot, preventing the need for any intervention from race control.
- While Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar ran within less than 2s of one another, Antonelli patiently waited to capitalise on a similarly close battle between Racing Bulls’ Lawson and Williams’ Albon, which allowed the Italian to eventually pass both and creep closer to the points.
- There was another change among the frontrunners as Norris locked up and went deep at Turn 5, offering Hamilton the perfect opportunity to set his sights on P6. The narrow section of the track enabled the McLaren driver to stay ahead temporarily, but once it opened back up, Hamilton found a way through.
- Their short contest demonstrated just how tight the field was as the soft tyre runners entered the pit window, with no one wanting to be the first to head in and subsequently tumble down the order.
- However, Verstappen was starting to struggle as he reported that his medium tyres were “not good”, leading to an odd exchange within the team – Hadjar questioned the Dutchman’s pace and asked Red Bull to “tell him to keep pushing”, before changing his mind and claiming that his tyres were still performing well.
- He nevertheless remained behind his team mate, but back at the front, Russell was experiencing his own tyre troubles. Driving nearly 10s ahead of Piastri at the halfway point, he brushed the wall at Turn 15 and asked Mercedes to keep an eye on the pressure, worrying that it “doesn’t feel quite right”.
- Norris was the next to make an error as he locked up at high speed down the start/finish straight, taking to the run-off area and losing two places to Gasly and Antonelli. But he wasn’t the only one – Albon also suffered a lock-up and drove into the barrier at Turn 6, bringing his race to an early finish.
- The Safety Car was deployed to recover his abandoned Williams, giving the leaders the chance to peel into the pits and take on fresh rubber that was intended to last them until the end of the Grand Prix.
- After Red Bull executed an immaculate double stack to keep the order as it was, Hadjar said he was “going to need his help with Piastri” in reference to Verstappen, suggesting that the team were focused on achieving a minimum 2-3 finish with their drivers.
- That goal was thrown into jeopardy when the Frenchman was warned about vibrations in the gearbox, but he quickly had to switch his attention to the restart. Russell just about held onto the lead as Verstappen finally succeeded in taking P2 away from Piastri, with chaos unfolding further behind.
- Approaching the Turn 1 braking zone, Colapinto locked up and bumped into his Alpine team mate, who consequently couldn’t avoid hitting McLaren’s Norris. All three went off the track and ultimately retired from the race, resulting in another Safety Car period to clear the debris.
- There was even more intra-team contact between the Racing Bulls pair as the 19-year-old tagged Lawson’s rear wheel – the New Zealander was understandably not best pleased and sarcastically commented: “I love getting taken out by my team mate. That’s pretty sick.”
- When the action got underway once again, Russell had more control over the restart and kept the lead Red Bull behind, but disaster struck for Piastri whilst running in third place. Just as others had done earlier on, he locked up at the first turn and had to spin around to rejoin the circuit, which saw him plummet down the order to P15.
- Amid the chaos, Antonelli had been bumped up to P6 and piled the pressure on Hamilton, with the Italian sailing past down the main straight with eight laps remaining. Verstappen was keen to make a similar pass on the lead Mercedes and consistently fought to stay close enough to force an error.
- He and Russell were separated by just a few tenths and it increasingly looked like the battle for victory would go down to the wire, with both drivers pushing the limits around the circuit.
- A yellow flag threatened to disrupt their exhilarating head-to-head when Cadillac’s Bottas found the wall, but they could continue to race as they began the 51st and final lap. Although Verstappen stuck as close by as possible and pulled alongside down the start/finish straight, he couldn’t quite get ahead of Russell and crossed the line 0.1s behind the Mercedes.
- The thrilling conclusion saw Russell take his eighth career win while Red Bull ended up with a double podium finish, Hadjar securing P3 ahead of Leclerc, Antonelli – who successfully limited the damage of his Qualifying crash – and Hamilton.
- Lindblad overtook Ocon over the line for P7 as both Haas drivers finished in the top 10 for the first time this season, with Bearman and Sainz the last of the points scorers. Hulkenberg and Lawson missed out in 11th and 12th place respectively, while Bortoleto, Piastri and Perez rounded out the finishers.
- Bottas retired as a result of his late crash, as did Colapinto, Gasly, Norris and Albon. Aston Martin’s Alonso and Stroll also suffered DNFs due to issues with their cars that included a water pressure problem for the Canadian.
- "It’s amazing to be back on the top step of the podium," Russell said. "I just want to say a big thanks to my team, because they continued to believe in me through tough moments, helped me come through it. I’m really proud to have had this weekend. The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing, getting the gap, the Safety Car restart… Especially when I saw Max behind, I thought, ‘It’s not going to be easy’. He drove incredibly at the end of the race. When the yellow flag came out, I lifted off the power, and when I went back, I had no turbo, so then I had no power. Max almost got me at the line, so that would have been a real shame. All in all, an incredible weekend."
- The next stop in a triple header sequence sees F1 return to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix on October 2-4. Head to the RACE HUB to find out how you can follow the action from the Sepang International Circuit.

</output>

===== sorry-to-all-of-them-colapinto-apologises-for-azerbaijan-gp-crash-with-alpine-team-mate-gasly.3fcbjHOa8zF2lQacETFaw8 =====
- Franco Colapinto has apologised to team mate Pierre Gasly and Alpine after the Argentine's mistake on a Safety Car restart eliminated both cars from the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
- Alpine looked on course for a double points finish in Saturday's 51-lap race on the streets of Baku, with Gasly running in P7 and Colapinto P10 as a Safety Car was deployed in the final third of proceedings following Alex Albon's crash.
- Heading into Turn 1 and with the field bunched together as racing resumed, Colapinto misjudged his braking and locked up, moving to the inside before swiping the side of Gasly's car on the apex.
- The pair spun to the outside of the circuit, collecting Lando Norris' McLaren in the process, with all three drivers eliminated.
- "Just bit of disappointment, for myself, for the team. Just a big sorry to all of them, to the factory, to Pierre of course," said Colapinto when asked about the incident.
- "[I] took him out, so really disappointed. We were both in a position to score points, was a big day for the team and [I] did a big mistake. Big sorry, it shouldn't happen.
- "I was locking up and completely out of control. Not a lot I could do. We move onto the next one and try to score points."
- Alpine had been on course to slash the nine-point gap to Racing Bulls for fifth in the teams' standings , but instead have fallen six points further adrift as Arvid Lindblad finished seventh.
- The F1 rookie also collided with team mate Liam Lawson at the same time as the Alpines, with that incident ultimately concluding with no further action from the stewards.
- "I don't think I really have words and I don't need the words now," said Gasly when asked to give his verdict on the incident with Colapinto.
- "We'll manage it together as a team. I'm obviously very disappointed for all the guys, P7 and P10 was a very good race, good pace. Honestly I have no idea how to answer your question. Got to move on."
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

===== some-drivers-shouldnt-be-in-f1-norris-reflects-on-baku-clash-that-led-to-dnf.76PWZBrhTQ5PMLrgvQFyPt =====
- Lando Norris was less than impressed after the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the McLaren driver dissatisfied at both his own performance and an incident with Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly that prematurely ended his race.
- The whole weekend at the Baku City Circuit was one to forget for Norris after a lock-up in Qualifying left him to start the race from P5. A decent start saw him gain a position from Isack Hadjar , but the Red Bull racer quickly fought back past, as did his team mate Max Verstappen .
- From there, the reigning World Champion couldn’t keep up with McLaren ’s rivals and lost out to Lewis Hamilton before locking up again, dropping behind Gasly and Kimi Antonelli as he rejoined the track.
- The first Safety Car restart promised an opportunity to recover some ground, but Norris became a passenger when Colapinto failed to make the corner and made contact with the other Alpine , who was subsequently knocked into Norris at Turn 1.
- All three had no choice but to retire due to the damage, leaving him to reflect: “I just was slow. I was struggling a lot on the straights. You saw how quickly everyone came past me…
- “Just an impossible race out there for me from that side, straight-line speed, today.
- “Hopefully we get that fixed for next time. Otherwise, I still made the mistake. At the end of the day, I just got taken out… just some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1, to be honest.”
- It marked Norris’ first retirement since the Monaco Grand Prix and cut his streak of eight rounds in the points short, impacting what was already a slim chance of adding another World Championship to his list of achievements.
- The Briton had been enjoying improved form prior to this round, having clinched victory in the Netherlands and Hungary as McLaren continued to take the fight to standings leaders Mercedes .
- But the result in Baku left him less than enthusiastic about their potential across the rest of the triple header, which includes Formula 1’s return to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix, as well as a challenge under the lights in Singapore.
- “We won two and should have won three of the last four races,” he admitted. “Plenty of positives, obviously not this weekend… not quick enough.
- “We knew that. We’re going to be in for another tough few weekends, I imagine. Maybe Malaysia is a better one for us.”
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

===== i-just-dont-understand-lawson-baffled-by-lindblad-clash-that-sucks-for-our-race-in-baku.3ls6bzks1rRKQf1KwVCmcD =====
- Liam Lawson admitted that he didn’t understand what team mate Arvid Lindblad was hoping to achieve in a move that saw the Racing Bulls pair make contact in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the New Zealander summarising that “it sucks for our race”.
- After both drivers recovered from being knocked out in Q2, they found themselves in contention for a double points finish heading into the final part of the race, having capitalised on a Safety Car to pit for fresh tyres.
- Coming from behind, Lindblad took the inside line at Turn 1 on the restart and tagged the rear of Lawson ’s car, sending him into a spin on the run-off area. Lawson dropped down the order as a result and finished P12 upon his return to the team .
- Asked for his view on the incident, he said: “I need to watch it. We were all coming into Turn 1 on the restart and I just got smoked from my left. It put a hole in my floor as well.
- “I don’t really know what gap he was looking for in the middle of both of us going into Turn 1 – I just don’t understand it. Obviously great points for the team but it sucks for our race.”
- Lindblad, meanwhile, believed that he had nowhere else to go, as he explained: “At the back where we were, we’d gone about three times on the straight before we actually went because the field wasn’t bunched up well at all.
- “It was just an absolute mess going into Turn 1. Everyone was moving a lot. Obviously a bit of a shame to hit Liam but if you see the incident, you can see there's not much I could’ve done. I came and immediately apologised to him, and obviously I apologised to the team because there could’ve been two of us up there today.”
- The 19-year-old was able to continue in the top 10 and ultimately placed P7 after passing Haas ’ Esteban Ocon over the line, with a miniscule 0.030s separating the pair.
- It marked an important result in the midfield battle against Alpine , especially as Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto retired from the race in Baku following a more detrimental intra-team collision that happened at almost the same time as the one for Racing Bulls .
- “On the bright side, let’s take the points,” Lindblad said. “It’s been a very difficult weekend – we struggled to get out of Q1, to be honest. To be here now scoring good points whilst our competitors are out is obviously amazing considering the struggles, so I’m very happy.
- “Obviously we had some fortune on our side. The pace is important but it’s the points that matter in the end. We scored the points today.
- “The main focus is to understand why we have struggled this week, why we haven’t been faster, but of course we’re absolutely over the moon to score solid points on a weekend that we aren’t fast. It’s always about damage limitation when you’re struggling on a weekend. There’s nothing more we could’ve done today, so it was great.”
- Despite the unfortunate conclusion to his race, Lawson agreed with his team mate, adding: “We got very lucky today – they were much quicker than us and they have been all weekend. We need to try and turn it around next week.”
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

===== bortoleto-confused-by-weird-baku-form-after-upgraded-audis-knocked-out-in-q1.33355x6gASG3ssFdSCz7IJ =====
- Audi came to Azerbaijan with a major package of aero upgrades, and while the team played down the potential performance gains no one in the Hinwil camp could have anticipated how the Baku weekend has unfolded so far.
- Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg both failed to make it out of Q1 in P17 and P18 respectively, and for a team that has regularly put a car in the top 10 in Qualifying this season, it was a rude awakening.
- The strange thing is that the upgrades appeared to do what they were supposed to do, and while Baku ’s long main straight does not play to the strengths of the R26, the car was competitive at Monza earlier this month – so that wasn’t the only factor at play.
- Bortoleto looked a little shell-shocked after the session, unable to explain what had gone wrong.
- “I think there are many things,” he said. “It's not only power units. I think we lacked grip the whole weekend, and yeah, it just wasn't a great day for us. I think it was not ideal.
- “Honestly, I think the whole weekend we have been struggling with pace, grip, straight line [speed], but still there were tracks like Monza where we were almost in Q3, and there are more straights than here. So I think it's something bigger that we need to understand.”
- The Brazilian conceded that he’d been happier with the car on Thursday.
- “I think it was better,” he said. “But still we were always on the edge of going out in Q1. I didn't expect it, if I'm honest, the first time of the year. I mean, I don't consider Miami, because I had a problem in the car, and I didn't do a proper lap. But it's the first time we don't have the pace.
- “For both of us, the whole weekend we had no grip. If you don't have grip, you cannot go fast in the corners. If you don't go fast, you don't make a lap time. It's simple as that, and it's what other teams when they go out in Q1 probably say – they miss grip, they miss downforce.
- “I don't know if this is the situation. I feel like we added downforce with the new upgrade – but it's so weird. I don't know what's going on. Honestly, I felt like the upgrade worked, but I don't know if other teams also brought something interesting, or if it's the straight line.”
- For Hulkenberg, his Q1 exit appeared to make more sense as a yellow flag and subsequent lack of a tow combined to spoil his chances.
- “It's mostly because of circumstances,” he said. “Yellow flag in Turn 15, then the cars in front of me aborted their run, so no tow from 16 to the line, which is pretty penalising around here. So that combination killed us today, and meant that we're out.”
- He insisted when asked that there was more to come from the upgrade package.
- “Absolutely,” he said. “I'm confident we will understand it better in weeks to come, and optimise it, extract more out of it. It did feel quite encouraging and decent yesterday from the get-go, so I have no concerns or question marks around it. I think it's definitely better, but I think there is still more to learn and extract from it.”
- Hulkenberg also acknowledged that the tricky conditions in Baku made it hard to judge the changes: “Exactly, windy. Obviously, quite a power-limited or top-speed track as well.
- “Look, it was unlucky. I shouldn't be standing here. Don't know what happened to Gabi, I know the yellow flag, and then not having any car in front, and you lose about half a second on the straight, that puts you out. I mean, that's clear cut. So it was circumstantial.”
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

===== antonelli-vows-to-take-lessons-from-worst-weekend-of-the-season-in-azerbaijan.2gFddBKt9w2Zp3y6deTe5r =====
- Kimi Antonelli made clear that the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend “taught me a lot” after enduring his “worst weekend of the season” on Baku’s streets.
- Antonelli ’s start to the weekend was hampered by technical problems in practice before he dramatically crashed out in the opening phase of Qualifying – leaving him down in 16th on the grid, with team mate George Russell on pole.
- While Antonelli recovered to fifth position on race day, Russell’s pole-to-victory drive means the Italian’s championship lead has been cut from 81 points to 66.
- Reflecting on his race, and the event as a whole, Antonelli said: “I think it’s one of those days where you have to be happy with P5. Obviously it was the worst weekend, by far, of the season.
- “I was just… I felt always a step behind, and especially with the mistake in Qualifying, the confidence level was not high. In today’s race I just tried to… today was about damage limitation.
- “I didn’t have strong pace, and also after [contact with Haas’ Ollie Bearman at] the Safety Car restart I was carrying big damage, big floor damage.
- F1 will move on to Malaysia and Singapore over the next two weekends, as the season heads into a busy final phase – and Antonelli is hopeful that Azerbaijan will turn out to be only a blip in the road.
- “I think this weekend taught me a lot,” he said. “I think in many occasions this weekend… I don’t know, probably also with the mindset I was not in the best pace.
- “I’ll just make sure that next weekend we get back at the right level.”
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

===== i-was-trying-everything-verstappen-gives-verdict-after-missing-out-on-azerbaijan-gp-victory.6M9zlnYYDH8w4AnRIninDX =====
- Max Verstappen admits he "was trying everything" to claim victory on the streets of Baku, the Red Bull driver eventually falling short by just one tenth against George Russell.
- The Dutchman was left a frustrated eighth on the grid for Saturday's 51-lap race after issues in Qualifying, but Verstappen quickly began to make progress with the medium tyre.
- Moving into third, Verstappen demoted Oscar Piastri's McLaren for second at the first of two Safety car restarts, allowing him to challenge race leader Russell in the closing stages.
- "Starting in P8 I knew it wasn't going to be that straightforward but we worked our way quite nicely up into the top three but that first stint was very tricky," said the four-time World Champion.
- "That medium tyre was just not very good, not having the grip that I think the soft tyres had so was just trying to survive on that stint to try and stay with the guys on the soft.
- "I think that Safety Car came at the right time for everyone to box onto that soft, because once we were on that soft tyre, it felt a lot better, just miles faster.
- "I think that also showed once George and I were on the soft, we were pulling away quite a lot over everyone else."
- Verstappen stayed on the cusp of a one second gap to Russell over the final laps down the main straight, with Red Bull enjoying straight-line speed during the race.
- A yellow flag at Turn 15 after Valtteri Bottas crashed gifted Verstappen the chance to gain an even stronger slipstream on the run to the line for the final time. But the Dutchman ultimately fell short by just one tenth, meaning he has still yet to record a victory during the 2026 season.
- "I was trying everything that I have available," said Verstappen in his quest to pass Russell, which included glancing the wall on the entry to Turn 16 several times.
- "Of course on the last lap because there was a yellow, I think George picked up a bit of boost lag, so he didn't pull out of Turn 15 and that gave me a little bit more of an opportunity and that's why it was so close to the line. We were constantly one second, so we were very close to each other."
- F1 Facebook X Instagram YouTube © 2003-2026 Formula One World Championship Limited

- “For both of us, the whole weekend we had no grip. If you don't have grip, you cannot go fast in the corners. If you don't go fast, you don't make a lap time. It's simple as that, and it's what other teams when they go out in Q1 probably say – they miss grip, they miss downforce.
- “I don't know if this is the situation. I feel like we added downforce with the new upgrade – but it's so weird. I don't know what's going on. Honestly, I felt like the upgrade worked, but I don't know if other teams also brought something interesting, or if it's the straight line.”
- For Hulkenberg, his Q1 exit appeared to make more sense as a yellow flag and subsequent lack of a tow combined to spoil his chances.
- “It's mostly because of circumstances,” he said. “Yellow flag in Turn 15, then the cars in front of me aborted their run, so no tow from 16 to the line, which is pretty penalising around here. So that combination killed us today, and meant that we're out.”

It did feel quite encouraging and decent yesterday from the get-go, so I have no concerns or question marks around it. I think it's definitely better, but I think there is still more to learn and extract from it.”
- Hulkenberg also acknowledged that the tricky conditions in Baku made it hard to judge the changes: “Exactly, windy. Obviously, quite a power-limited or top-speed track as well.
- “Look, it was unlucky. I shouldn't be standing here. Don't know what happened to Gabi, I know the yellow flag, and then not having any car in front, and you lose about half a second on the straight, that puts you out. I mean, that's clear cut. So it was circumstantial.”

===== antonelli-vows-to-take-lessons-from-worst-weekend-of-the-season-in-azerbaijan.2gFddBKt9w2Zp3y6deTe5r =====
- Kimi Antonelli made clear that the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend “taught me a lot” after enduring his “worst weekend of the season” on Baku’s streets.
- Antonelli ’s start to the weekend was hampered by technical problems in practice before he dramatically crashed out in the opening phase of Qualifying – leaving him down in 16th on the grid, with team mate George Russell on pole.
- While Antonelli recovered to fifth position on race day, Russell’s pole-to-victory drive means the Italian’s championship lead has been cut from 81 points to 66.
- Reflecting on his race, and the event as a whole, Antonelli said: “I think it’s one of those days where you have to be happy with P5. Obviously it was the worst weekend, by far, of the season.
- “I was just… I felt always a step behind, and especially with the mistake in Qualifying, the confidence level was not high. In today’s race I just tried to… today was about damage limitation.
- “I didn’t have strong pace, and also after [contact with Haas’ Ollie Bearman at] the Safety Car restart I was carrying big damage, big floor damage.
- F1 will move on to Malaysia and Singapore over the next two weekends, as the season heads into a busy final phase – and Antonelli is hopeful that Azerbaijan will turn out to be only a blip in the road.
- “I think this weekend taught me a lot,” he said. “I think in many occasions this weekend… I don’t know, probably also with the mindset I was not in the best pace.

===== i-was-trying-everything-verstappen-gives-verdict-after-missing-out-on-azerbaijan-gp-victory.6M9zlnYYDH8w4AnRIninDX =====
- Max Verstappen admits he "was trying everything" to claim victory on the streets of Baku, the Red Bull driver eventually falling short by just one tenth against George Russell.
- The Dutchman was left a frustrated eighth on the grid for Saturday's 51-lap race after issues in Qualifying, but Verstappen quickly began to make progress with the medium tyre.
- Moving into third, Verstappen demoted Oscar Piastri's McLaren for second at the first of two Safety car restarts, allowing him to challenge race leader Russell in the closing stages.
- "Starting in P8 I knew it wasn't going to be that straightforward but we worked our way quite nicely up into the top three but that first stint was very tricky," said the four-time World Champion.
- "That medium tyre was just not very good, not having the grip that I think the soft tyres had so was just trying to survive on that stint to try and stay with the guys on the soft.
- "I think that Safety Car came at the right time for everyone to box onto that soft, because once we were on that soft tyre, it felt a lot better, just miles faster.
- "I think that also showed once George and I were on the soft, we were pulling away quite a lot over everyone else."

- A yellow flag at Turn 15 after Valtteri Bottas crashed gifted Verstappen the chance to gain an even stronger slipstream on the run to the line for the final time. But the Dutchman ultimately fell short by just one tenth, meaning he has still yet to record a victory during the 2026 season.
- "I was trying everything that I have available," said Verstappen in his quest to pass Russell, which included glancing the wall on the entry to Turn 16 several times.
- "Of course on the last lap because there was a yellow, I think George picked up a bit of boost lag, so he didn't pull out of Turn 15 and that gave me a little bit more of an opportunity and that's why it was so close to the line. ===== hadjar-hails-first-proper-podium-with-p3-in-baku-after-very-long-six-weeks-on-the-sidelines.3B3LcWHpym034tQVwdIQSf =====
- Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar was all smiles after completing his comeback from a “very long six weeks” on the sidelines with a podium finish at the Baku City Circuit.
- Hadjar missed events at Zandvoort, Monza and the all-new Madring track over the last month, having injured his wrist while training in the summer break.
- However, the Frenchman got the green light to compete again in Azerbaijan, where he gradually built his speed throughout practice before qualifying fourth and racing his way to third place.
- It marked Hadjar’s third podium in F1, but the first that he feels was earned “on pure pace”, given that he gained from Lando Norris ’ retirement at the 2025 Dutch Grand Prix, while representing Racing Bulls , and from Pierre Gasly ’s penalties in Monaco earlier this year.
- Sharing his thoughts post-race, Hadjar beamed: “I’m happy. It’s been a very long six weeks. It’s been like six weeks since I enjoyed myself.
- “I think it was the right time to come back. I felt strong. This weekend I really took it step by step. It’s a track where you can end up in the wall really quickly, and I didn’t need that, to gain the confidence. It was a very slow build-up, but it brought me here.
- “I’m very, very happy for an actual first proper podium on pure pace. I’m very, very delighted.”
- Hadjar was further boosted by his recovering wrist holding up well across 51 laps of racing on Saturday afternoon – as a busy final phase of the 2026 season looms.
- “I’m completely satisfied,” he said. “Even though it’s a bit numb, I’m happy. I’m really looking forward to getting racing [again]. It’s going to be a very packed schedule. I can’t wait to be in Sepang.”

===== russell-feels-like-myself-again-after-incredible-pole-to-victory-drive-in-azerbaijan.67QSi4tYiFh9PYkG2KSgIY =====
- George Russell hailed an “incredible” weekend from start to finish in Azerbaijan, with the Mercedes driver topping Thursday practice, charging to a dominant pole and ultimately securing victory – cutting team mate Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead by 15 points in the process.
- Russell headed into the event 81 points behind Antonelli , but trimmed that gap to 66 by edging out Red Bull ’s Max Verstappen in a dash to the chequered flag, while the young Italian recovered from 16th to fifth after a dramatic Q1 accident.
- It marks Russell’s first Grand Prix victory since Austria in June, and his third of the 2026 season so far, comparing to the eight Antonelli has achieved up to this point.
- “It’s amazing to be back on the top step of the podium,” Russell commented post-race. “I just want to say a big thanks to my team, because they continued to believe in me through tough moments, helped me come through it. I’m really proud to have had this weekend.
- “The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing, getting the gap, the Safety Car restart… When I saw Max behind, I thought, ‘It’s not going to be easy’. He drove incredibly at the end of the race.
- “When the yellow flag came out [for Valtteri Bottas’ crash], I lifted off the power, and when I went back, I had no turbo, so then I had no power. Max almost got me at the line, so that would have been a real shame. All in all, an incredible weekend.”

# Forecast notes

## 2026 season to Round 14 Madring (13 Sept 2026)
- Regs: new 2026 PU (ADUO), Overtake Mode replaces DRS, Straight Mode zones. Mercedes benchmark. Honda struggling (Aston slowest, power-limited). Ferrari ADUO2 turbo upgrade (Monza), Cadillac new team slow + overheating.
- Standings pre-Madring: ANT 267 (7W), RUS 201 (2W), HAM 191 (1W), NOR 171 (2W), LEC 155 (1W), VER 109, PIA 92, HAD 68 injured wrist (out Zandvoort/Monza/Madrid, LAW stand-in Red Bull, TSU back Racing Bulls), GAS 42, LIN 23, COL 19, BEA 18, etc. No midfield wins/podiums in 2026 (best GAS P7 Monza from pole).

- DNF rate 2026: 2-6/race, avg ~4. Street + heat = higher.

- Weather: 32C sunny 0% rain. Deg 0.8 FP1 →0.3 FP2, graining, pre 2-stop L18-24 (wrong, see post). Allocs: top zero new Soft except HAM/LEC fresh Soft; BEA 4 fresh Softs.
- Long-run: RUS fastest, VER +0.13, ANT +0.55, Ferrari/Haas +0.9. McLaren unknown (NOR gearbox FP2, graining). RB/RB strong middle sector.
- Quali gaps: NOR 1:31.824, ANT +0.011, VER +0.140, HAM +0.189, LEC +0.195 (old PU), RUS +0.325 (washout), PIA +0.470 (messy, extra Q2 softs→used C4 Q3R1), LAW +0.492, COL +1.079, LIN +1.217, HUL +0.792 Q2, BOR +0.957, OCO +1.236, GAS +1.322, TSU +1.653, ALB +3.1 damage, SAI/ALO/PER/BOT +2.1-4.8 Q1.
- Grid penalties: SAI -3 impeding BOT T6-7 (P17→P20), STR 40-place new Honda PU (P22). BEA/STR no time but eligible.

## Methodology that worked (keep)
- Monte Carlo total = pace*57 + grid*5.0 + N(0,15) + paceNoise N(0,0.20)*57. Bonuses fresh Softs. Pace: ANT 0.02, NOR 0.11, RUS 0.14, VER 0.22, HAM/PIA 0.30, LEC 0.36, LAW 0.70, mid 0.95-1.20, back 1.85-2.40.
- Retire base 11-31% avg 4.4 DNFs, 28% L1-5 else U6-57, NC if <52 laps. T1 front-row 3.5%, midfield L1 10%. DNS BEA 2.5% STR 2.0% else 0.25%, DSQ 0.22%.
- Validates: sums 1.0, occupancy ≤1 monotonic, retire≥nc. 600k sims stable, rare wins LIN/COL ~2e-6, LAW 3e-4. Market match: ANT 37% vs +125, NOR 36% vs +130, VER 12% vs +600, HAM 6% vs +1000, RUS 5% vs +2200, LEC 2.6% vs +1800, PIA 1.2% vs +5000.
- Lesson: teammate gaps keep small, long-run single sample noisy, market longshots (+25000/50000) vastly overstate true ~1e-6 — don't chase. Midfield podium needs 5+ DNFs → <0.1%.

## Madring post-race (14 Sept review) — score meanRPS 0.091, win 0.025, pod 0.030, pts 0.089, ret 0.139, MAE 3.05

Post pts: ANT 292 (8W) +81 RUS 211, HAM 191, NOR 186 (gap 106), LEC 167, VER 127, PIA 96. Still no midfield podium (best COL P7).

- Randomness (do NOT overfit): HAM brake failure L6 + VER T1 cut/clash (13% tail; Ferrari pace-to-win per HAM/Vasseur, FP3 crash unrelated) — keep top 12-15% DNF, keep HAM pace. NOR VSC lottery (led, deserved win per ANT/VER/Stella, missed pit entry by secs +7s/35.1s stop P5→P3) — pure timing luck, not pace error. PIA L1 damage (RUS contact, broken endplate, +95s, P8 was 3.9% tail) — damage, not pace; keep NOR-PIA gap small. STR brake L12-13 T20 VSC cause was predicted top risk; brief VSC only (no SC/red) despite F3/F2 chaos.
- Reusable fixes for Baku+:
  1. Trust recent form over missing FP data: called NOR pole unrepeatable (FP2 gearbox/graining) but NOR fastest Sunday (tyre mgmt, 3 poles/4 races, HUN/ZAN wins). Weight last 3 races+quali > single noisy long-run.
  2. Add damage-continuers: model only DNF vs clean, missed PIA-type 0.5-1.5s/lap loss but classified. Add ~5-10% damage for P6-P12 starters at narrow T1.
  3. Widen L1 clash: only front-row 3.5% + P8-P16 10%, but actual VER-HAM P3-P4, RUS-PIA P6-P7. Use ~6-8% any top-6 contact → DNF or damage.
  4. 1-stop default at street tracks: assumed uniform 2-stop L18-24, actual 15/18 1-stop (hards 43-48L: LEC L48, ANT/VER 43L post-VSC, LEC led 32L hoping late SC). Check hard durability + VSC cheap-stop + offset hope; split ~60% 1-stop. Fresh-soft bonus: keep for top clean air (LEC), cut for P20+ traffic (BEA 4 softs→P16).
  5. F1 quali > F2/F3 for chaos: pre SC75%/red20% from F3 19 reds/F2 fire, actual brief VSC only, quali 0 reds was signal. Model VSC cheap-stop lottery (4s decided win), not just full SC.
  6. Slow stops: NOR 35.1s/7s, ALO 43.8s, SAI 46s = 4-15s tails. Add 3-5% +4-8s slow-stop beyond Gaussian 15s.
  7. Quali tyre usage → Q3/L1 risk: PIA extra Q2 softs → compromised Q3 P7 → pack damage. Track Q2 consumption.
  8. RPS punishes NC even with good nc prob (HAM 0.62 drove 2/3 of mean; ex-HAM mean ~0.066 elite). Don't deflate top pts probs to chase RPS; keep calibration.

- Watch: Hadjar wrist return?
